C-46; Alberta Business Corporations Act (ABCA), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9; Alberta Business Corporations Regulation, Alta. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or competent national civil registry of the holder's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, Canadian sanctions regulations issued under SEMA and the United Nations Act, FINTRAC's domestic AML/CFT registry, and Alberta Securities Commission enforcement records. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person (PEP), foreign or domestic, including verification of source of funds and beneficial ownership. Screening results must be documented and retained in accordance with FINTRAC record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry; Corporate Registry Service, Service Alberta (online through albertacorporate.com and Alberta Corporate Register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name may be in English, French, or both, and must include a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd. or Limitée. Names using non-Latin scripts require a transliteration into the corporate register and must be searchable in the NUANS (North American Numbering and Uniform System) database. The name must not be misleading or contrary to public policy under the ABCA and applicable name regulations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: or any other word implying a regulated profession or governmental connection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant may request a written reconsideration from the Alberta Corporate Registry within 30 days, providing evidence of prior entitlement, written consents from affected name holders, or clarification of the proposed corporate name. Where the rejection is based on a statutory or ministerial determination, an administrative appeal may be filed under the ABCA and the Governing Name Regulation. The applicant may also perform a new NUANS search and file a fresh name reservation. All appeal filings must be submitted through Service Alberta with the prescribed fee and supporting documentation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office acceptance is generally permitted for a low-risk digital video game publisher, provided the registered office is a real physical address in Alberta at which service of process may be effected and from which corporate records may be accessed. A virtual mail-forwarding service alone does not satisfy the ABCA registered office obligation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated below a 5% annual likelihood for a non-regulated digital publisher carrying on business through Steam and console storefronts. FINTRAC, Service Alberta, or corporate registry compliance audits remain possible in the ordinary course.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9 (Alberta), as amended; sections 6 (incorporation), 9 (articles), 12 (certificate), 14 (registered office), 101-102 (directors), and 109 (officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Corporate Registry and Companies Division)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, together with initial Notice of Registered Office Address and Notice of Directors
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; initial capitalization may be as low as CAD 1 (e.g., 100 common shares at CAD 0.01 per share), and no escrow, deposit, or bank confirmation is required for a standard Alberta Business Corporation engaged in digital software publishing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's subscription for 100 common shares at CAD 0.01 per share be accepted, the initial paid-up capital be CAD 1, and share certificates be issued accordingly. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at [Registered Office Address], Alberta, and the corporate records be maintained there. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed sole director. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each to hold office until the next annual meeting. RESOLVED, that the minute book be opened and all acts conforming to the Alberta Business Corporations Act be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized Corporate Registry service providers operating the Service Alberta online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request and obtain a NUANS (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) report for up to three proposed corporate names; verify the distinctive element (e.g., Aurora Byte Interactive) and the legal element (Inc. or Corp.); confirm the absence of prohibited, reserved, or confusingly similar names for use in Alberta.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (up to three, in priority order)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first proposed name is refused, the second or third name from the same NUANS report may be used; the search report supports a name reservation for up to 90 days. A new search is required only if all three proposed names are rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — online incorporation filing through Service Alberta or an authorized Alberta Corporate Registry service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute the Articles of Incorporation setting out the corporate name, registered office address in Alberta, share structure (including unlimited Common Shares), restrictions on share transfer (if any), the number or minimum and maximum number of directors, and the incorporators' declarations. File the executed Articles together with the NUANS report and the prescribed incorporation fee through the registry's online system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency or correction notice, the applicant must refile corrected Articles within the stated cure period (usually 60 days); fees are generally forfeited only if the application is formally abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Consolidated Corporate Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Certificate and Corporate Extract Division)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following approval, the registry endorses and files the Articles and issues a Certificate of Incorporation dated as of the endorsement. Obtain the Consolidated Corporate Extract (status certificate) verifying the legal name, incorporation number, registered office, and current directors; this document constitutes prima facie evidence of corporate existence for banks and payment platforms such as Steam Valve and PlayStation Store.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and director information as filed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate or Corporate Extract contains an error, apply to the registry for a certificate of correction or articles of correction under the Business Corporations Act; legal name corrections are typically made by articles of correction rather than re-incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance — By-Law No. 1, First Board Meeting, and Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the Corporation / Corporate Secretary (internal statutory governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting of directors or execute written resolutions in lieu of meeting; adopt By-Law No. 1 covering borrowing powers, banking, quorum, and meeting procedures; approve the pro-forma First Board Resolution for share subscription, adoption of registered office, and appointment of officers; issue share certificates to the subscribers and open the corporate minute book, securities register, and directors register.
required_dossiers: Minute book and corporate seal (if adopted)
Share certificates and register of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director quorum cannot be convened in person, a written consent resolution signed by all directors is legally equivalent to a meeting; if a corporate seal is unavailable, signing by an officer and one director is sufficient under the by-law and the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Non-Mandatory Industrial and Environmental Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing authority (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton), Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the physical office location mandates a municipal business licence and apply under the appropriate business class. Confirm that digital software publishing (NAICS 511210, ISIC 5820) is not a provincially licenced trade under the Licensing of Trades and Businesses Regulation; arrange for e-waste recycling compliance for decommissioned computer equipment and ensure the leased premises comply with fire safety and OHS clearance before employees occupy the workplace.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licence)
Certificate of Incorporation and Consolidated Corporate Extract
Lease agreement or landlord consent for business use
Employer OHS registration and first-aid records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipal business licence is refused on zoning or use-classification grounds, re-file under a permitted home-based or office use class, request a variance, or appeal to the municipal subdivision and development appeal board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — software publishing via digital stores (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210) is not a designated licenced activity under the Alberta Licensing of Trades and Businesses Regulation (Alta Reg 203/2007); municipal business licensing authorities remain relevant for physical office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral manufacturing or operating licence is required; a general municipal business licence may be required by the municipality where the registered or administrative office is located.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c. E-12
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based digital publishing operations are not listed as mandatory EIA activities under Schedule 1; no registration or full EIA report is triggered absent physical manufacturing, processing, or waste-generating industrial operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or stack emission limits apply to pure software publishing; general municipal sewer use bylaws govern sanitary discharges; decommissioned IT equipment must be managed through the Electronics Recycling Regulation (Alta Reg 76/2011) and, if hazardous, under the Waste Control Regulation (Alta Reg 192/1996).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and building occupancy certification under the Alberta Fire Code and municipal building inspection; structural load approval for the leased premises; employer registration with the Workers' Compensation Board — Alberta and workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c. O-2, including first-aid, ergonomic, and remote-employee compliance for office-based software staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; GST/HST and federal corporate income tax are administered centrally by CRA through the My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE portals. Alberta's provincial corporate income tax is administered by CRA under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement, and Alberta does not operate a separate provincial sales tax authority for GST/HST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Alberta Business Corporations Act and obtain the certificate of incorporation. Step 2 - Submit Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' to the CRA, available online through My Business Account or by fax/mail, and request program accounts: RP (federal/Alberta corporation income tax), RT (GST/HST), and RC (payroll) if employees are hired. CRA will issue a 9-digit Business Number (BN). Step 3 - For foreign-controlled entities, file the applicable T2 corporate return schedules and maintain non-resident shareholder information. Step 4 - If the entity is a non-resident supplier of remote digital goods to Canadian consumers, use the CRA's simplified non-resident GST/HST registration process even without a Canadian permanent establishment, once the CAD 30,000 remote-supply threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box or equivalent entity-classification election; a CBCA/ABCA business corporation is invariably taxed at entity level under both federal and Alberta income tax. Relevant statutory elections include: ITA s. 85(1) corporate rollover on incorporation/asset transfers; ITA s. 83(2) capital-dividend account election; GST/HST section 156 nil-consideration election for closely related registrants; and the foreign-affiliate dispositions and FAPI elections under ITA ss. 91-95. Hybrid mismatch rules are not elective: CRA applies ITA s. 18.4 and s. 20.2 to deny deductions where a payment is not included in the recipient's taxable income in its residence jurisdiction, aligning treatment by statutory rule rather than taxpayer classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) - federal GST of 5%; in Alberta, no provincial sales tax applies, so the effective indirect tax rate is 5% for supplies deemed to be made in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (or current quarter for new registrants) for any person making taxable supplies in Canada; for non-resident remote digital suppliers, CAD 30,000 of remote supplies to Canadian consumers in a 12-month period triggers mandatory simplified GST/HST registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not require real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices. GST/HST returns are filed electronically through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE service. Suppliers must retain readable electronic or paper records, including detailed platform payout reports from Steamworks and PlayStation Store, for six years. Invoices must display the supplier's Business Number and GST/HST registration number, but no electronic invoicing protocol is mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of digital game content by electronic communication is zero-rated if made to a non-resident individual or non-resident business that is outside Canada at the time of the supply and the supply is not received, used, or enjoyed in Canada. For Steam/PlayStation downloads, the publisher must rely on platform end-customer data (IP geolocation, billing address, country code, and account profile) to segregate Canadian-resident sales from exported sales. Zero-rating is denied where the recipient is in Canada or where the digital license is used or exploited in Canada. The exporter must hold credible contemporaneous records proving the recipient's non-resident status for every zero-rated transaction, including marketplace sales routed through Valve or Sony.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration Form B13A - required only for physical game media shipped out of Canada; not required for pure digital downloads
Digital invoice or sales contract specifying the non-resident customer, digital license grant, delivery method, and sale proceeds in CAD or USD
Steamworks payout report and/or PlayStation Store statement showing end-customer jurisdiction, platform fee, and net remittance to the publisher
Proof of inbound payment from outside Canada, such as SWIFT/remittance slips or Valve/Sony payout settlement records denominated in foreign currency
Customer geolocation evidence: IP address logs, billing country, and platform account residency declaration
Bill of lading or air waybill where physical console game media is exported to foreign warehouses or retail partners
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period, with an unlimited reassessment window for fraud or misrepresentation. If a zero-rated digital supply is recharacterized as made to a Canadian resident without GST/HST, the tax becomes payable with interest from the original filing date, and associated input tax credits on related costs may be clawed back. False or misleading statements attract a gross-negligence penalty of not less than CAD 250 and up to 25% of the understated net tax; deliberate evasion can lead to fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. Exporters must preserve the full documentation bundle and FX repatriation evidence for six years; the 180-day remittance benchmark is a commonly applied audit tolerance and transfer-pricing proxy, although no explicit GST statute imposes a strict 180-day repatriation deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating alongside the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision of Schedule I banks and FINTRAC for enforcement of cross-border electronic fund transfer reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada has no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration because the Foreign Exchange Control Act and its subordinate regulations were repealed in December 1951; the foreign exchange market is liberalized and centrally supervised by the Bank of Canada only for monetary and financial stability purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility exists on both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Canadian dollar is an internationally floating and freely deliverable currency, and no governmental authorization, exchange control permit, or conversion limit applies to USD-denominated revenues earned via Valve Steam and PlayStation digital store payouts. The only quantitative profit-remittance hurdle is the Part XIII non-resident withholding tax imposed by the Income Tax Act (Canada): the statutory rate is 25% on dividends and certain gross royalties paid by the Alberta corporation to foreign shareholders, reduced by applicable income tax treaties (Canada-US Convention: 5% for corporate shareholders owning at least 10% of voting stock, 15% otherwise; certain arm's-length royalty payments may be exempt or reduced under treaty provisions). Repatriation of equity capital is unrestricted. Procedural compliance requires filing CRA Forms NR4/NR4-Summary, obtaining a W-8BEN-E or NR301 treaty-residency certificate, and including the withholding certificate number in the remittance instructions to the clearing bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed holding period for export receipts in Canada. Digital video game sale proceeds received from Steam and PlayStation store payouts may be retained in USD, deposited into a non-resident or domestic USD operational account, converted into CAD at the corporation's discretion, or held offshore. The only applicable obligation is FINTRAC EFT reporting for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, plus regular CRA income reporting of the USD revenue at the Bank of Canada yearly average or transaction-date exchange rates. No Bank of Canada conversion certificate or export-validation document is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account plus Operational CAD and USD Corporate Treasury Account
Operational Corporate Account with USD Clearing Sub-ledger and Escrow Segregation Facilities
Operational Account with Commercial Letter of Credit and Trade Finance Facilities
Operational CAD/USD Account with Correspondent US Clearing Rail
Operational Account with International Correspondent Banking Network
Alberta Domestic Treasury Operational Account (Provincial Crown Corporation)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, and strictly auxiliary. FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses and international Electronic Money Institutions (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Stripe Treasury) can provide efficient payout-receipt rails for Steamworks and PlayStation Partner store settlements and can execute low-value disbursement runs to overseas contractors; however, under the Canadian Bank Act they are not authorized deposit-taking institutions, do not offer CDIC-insured deposit insurance, and operate through partner bank accounts with funds held in pooled segregation arrangements. Legal constraints include mandatory disclosure of uninsured status, US OFAC and Canadian sanctions-program filtering obligations, and heightened EDD treatment by any downstream correspondent bank. Optimal treasury architecture: use a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank as the primary liquidity and clearing hub, and retain at most one EMI rail as a contingency collection circuit for platform micro-payouts with a documented FINTRAC MSB registration and contractual fund-segregation opinion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for signing officers during the initial corporate account opening at the Big Six Canadian banks, unless remote video onboarding is approved for low-risk entities whose sole director is a Canadian resident. For the Alberta-incorporated video game publisher, if any director or authorized signatory is non-resident, the bank will normally require a certified passport copy, notarized board resolution, certificate of incumbency, and an in-person identity interview at a Canadian branch, Canadian consulate, or via a bank-designated remote video tool with heightened supervision. Canadian statutory law does not mandate physical presence for non-resident officers, but internal bank policies classify such mandates as enhanced due diligence triggers. A Canadian resident signing officer with existing personal banking history at the institution materially accelerates the process and may eliminate the in-branch interview for the remaining signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity where non-resident shareholders hold 25% or more of voting equity or control, especially through trusts, as the bank must resolve source-of-wealth for each beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Alberta Corporate Registry search report; formal UBO register maintained under the Canada Business Corporations Act and Alberta Business Corporations Act; CRS and FATCA self-certification forms (CRA forms and W-8/W-9 series) for each material UBO; notarized source-of-wealth letters; corporate organizational chart; constitutional documents (Articles of Incorporation, By-laws, unanimous shareholder agreement); and a board resolution identifying authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Platform payout concentration risk or transaction pattern mismatch where USD settlement amounts from Valve (Steam) and Sony (PlayStation) fluctuate by large technical volumes despite low payroll, causing the bank's transaction-monitoring system to flag first-year activity as unusual
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Steamworks distribution agreement and Sony PlayStation Partner developer agreement; platform payout statements and reconciliation ledgers mapping each store remittance to the treasury account; monthly internal management accounts; corporate AML/ATF policy demonstrating transaction monitoring under PCMLTFA; and a signed director's explanation letter describing the digital-goods revenue model and peak sale-season dynamics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment style disbursement requests where payments are directed to co-development studios, audio contractors, localization vendors, or overseas middleware licensors under names different from the primary platform counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed service, licensing, or co-development agreements for each payee; commercial invoices with vendor tax registration numbers (GST/HST or foreign equivalents); a board-approved disbursement matrix and payee KYC pack containing passport or corporate registry extract for each invited commercial payee; and detailed wire reference fields quoting invoice numbers and contract IDs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of any alternative settlement chain, such as funds routed from an EMI, digital wallet, or a non-bank payment processor, that may appear to the correspondent bank as an unregulated money transmission circuit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete source-of-funds trail from Steam/PlayStation platform statements directly into the Canadian banking account; a formal corporate statement confirming the treasury does not engage in cryptocurrency transactions; FINTRAC MSB registration certificate if any EMI rail is used; due-diligence file on the EMI's partner bank and получатель status; and legal opinion on fund segregation from a Canadian law firm if ambiguity persists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from a foreign parent or non-resident shareholders must be routed via SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfer (or MT202 COV where a cover payment is needed) to the Alberta corporation's account at a Schedule I Canadian bank, with final settlement in CAD through Lynx, Canada's ISO 20022 high-value payment system, or in USD through the bank's US correspondent (e.g., Fedwire/CHIPS credit into the bank's USD head-office account). The remitter-to-receiver information line must state the legal entity name exactly as it appears on the Alberta corporate registry, the CRA Business Number (BN), and a purpose code corresponding to the IMF Balance of Payments direct-investment equity category (e.g., 'EQ - equity injection / capital contribution'), thereby avoiding the AML rejection risk arising from abbreviations or third-party beneficiary references. Inbound electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC within required statutory timelines. No Bank of Canada approval or exchange-control documentation is required; the bank may, however, request a board resolution, subscribed-share certificate, or investment agreement to evidence the non-repayment nature of the capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for engine licensing fees, console platform SDK obligations, middleware royalties, localization services, and co-development retainers are cleared through four principal rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct remittance in USD or CAD with detailed remittance information referencing invoice numbers and the corporate creditor's bank details; (2) irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit, payable at sight or term, issued by the Canadian bank for high-value hardware, middleware, or distribution contracts exceeding material monetary thresholds; (3) ACSS (Automated Clearing Settlement System) or Lynx transfers for domestic Canadian-dollar disbursements; and (4) platform-level settlement where Steam and PlayStation store revenues are received directly from Valve and Sony into the treasury account, then fanned out to subcontractors. Payments to US-registered licensors are commonly executed in USD via Fedwire/CHIPS through the Canadian bank's correspondent; all beneficiaries must clear the institution's OFAC and Canadian Economic Sanctions filter, and each outbound transfer of CAD 10,000 or more is subject to FINTRAC EFT reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CAD spot and outright forward contracts traded with Schedule I Canadian Bank Act dealers (RBC, TD, BMO, CIBC, Scotiabank, National Bank) for hedging Steam and PlayStation USD revenue streams against CAD operating costs

Cross-currency swaps (fixed-floating USD/CAD) permitted for balance-sheet hedging of USD-denominated receivables, with ISDA and CSA documentation under Canadian Derivatives Law and central clearing through the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation where applicable

Vanilla FX options (call and put on USD/CAD) purchased from domestic authorized derivatives dealers, limited to a notional matching budgeted platform net revenue and accounted for under IFRS 9 hedge accounting rules

NDFs are not necessary and are generally non-permissible onshore because CAD is fully deliverable; offshore CAD non-deliverable forwards would be treated as non-compliant speculative instruments by Canadian corporate banks and are disallowed in the treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return to the Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the incorporation anniversary or extra-provincial registration anniversary; recurrence every 12 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative non-compliance notices; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to strike off or dissolve the corporation in the Alberta Gazette, with reinstatement possible only by court order or administrative conditions within the statutory period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return including Alberta corporate income tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; continued delinquency may trigger director liability, interest accrual, and criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return and remittance if annual filer status applies to the Steam/console publishing entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the corporation's fiscal-year end unless monthly or quarterly election is in effect
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Assessment of interest and penalties on unreported taxable supplies; gross-negligence penalties up to 50% of understated tax for intentional omissions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership and directors' information embedded in the Alberta Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the Alberta Annual Return, i.e., within one month after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or missing confirmation may result in administrative penalty, director disqualification measures, and inhibition or strike-off of the corporate registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, the corporation must appoint an independent auditor unless all shareholders consent in writing to dispense with the audit for the fiscal year; no asset or revenue threshold provides exemption. Public, distributing, or extra-provincial corporations generally cannot waive the auditor requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) Part II for private corporations; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Part I is required for public or publicly accountable enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the corporation must confirm the Register of Individuals with Significant Control is accurate and complete as part of the Alberta Annual Return. On any shareholding transfer or acquisition of significant control, the ISC register must be updated within 15 days of the corporation becoming aware; records of individuals with significant control must be retained for 6 years after they cease to have such control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 190–1,120 per year, depending on corporate agent services, mail forwarding, and compliance support in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–15,000 for a compact private PC/console game publishing entity, excluding complex consolidations of international Steam or PlayStation revenue streams

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: combined preferential rate of approximately 11% on active business income up to CAD 500,000 (federal 9%; Alberta 2%). No general statutory tax holiday for digital publishing. Federal SR&ED investment tax credits (15% refundable/35% refundable for qualifying CCPCs, as applicable) and, for eligible Alberta interactive digital media production and publishing expenditures, the Alberta Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit may reduce the effective provincial rate. Foreign tax credits and treaty relief are available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal form also used to compute Alberta corporate income tax); filed electronically through CRA Corporation Internet Filing / EFIL using approved tax software and accessible via CRA My Business Account. Alberta corporate tax is administered by the Canada Revenue Agency and integrated into the T2 return; no separate Alberta corporate income tax return is required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly corporate income tax instalments are required where net tax payable exceeds the CRA prescribed instalment threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Tax balance-due day is generally 2 months after fiscal year-end for non-CCPCs and 3 months for CCPCs eligible for the small business deduction. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada are subject to the same 6-month filing rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, jurisdiction of incorporation, fiscal year-end, mailing address, registered office, and authorized representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must enter the Canadian business number, Canadian permanent establishment address, and identify the corporation as non-resident; provide name and address of the Canadian filing agent or representative where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a – Type of Corporation / CCPC Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification as CCPC, other Canadian corporation, or non-resident corporation; determines eligibility for small business deduction and installment rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation controlled by non-residents cannot be a CCPC; therefore no small business deduction may be claimed. Non-resident corporations must mark the non-resident classification box and allocate income to Canadian permanent establishments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 – Aggregate Allocation of Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income among provinces and territories based on permanent establishment formulas; Alberta rate applies to the portion allocated to Alberta.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with an Alberta permanent establishment must complete the permanent establishment allocation schedule; only Canadian PE income is subject to Part I tax and provincial allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from financial statement net income to tax depreciation, capital gains, reserves, foreign accrual, transfer pricing adjustments, and non-capital loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source active business income attributable to the PE; recognise Steam/PlayStation revenue net of platform fees using GAAP; attach audited or reviewed financial statements as required and disclose related-party transactions with Valve or other platform owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes the CCPC small business deduction on active business income from qualifying Canadian-source business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned corporation generally cannot claim the SBD; no entry should be made unless the corporation qualifies as a CCPC under subsection 125(7).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents, including licensing, royalties, revenue sharing, cost contributions, loans, and advances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must report all controlled transactions involving Canadian PE income and attach contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation sufficient to satisfy section 247.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month late, up to 12 months. Repeated failures, false statements, or gross negligence attract additional penalties, including 50% of the understated tax under subsection 163(2), daily compounded arrears interest, and partial or complete loss of loss carryovers depending on the assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal Part XIII withholding tax on gross dividends paid by a resident Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder; Alberta does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Canadian payer a completed CRA Form NR301 together with a current certificate of residence (TRC) issued by the home tax authority before or at the time of payment. The payer retains the form and withholds at the treaty rate. If excess tax has been withheld, the non-resident may claim a refund using Form NR7 within the applicable limitation period. Under the Canada-U.S. treaty, for example, dividends to a U.S. corporate beneficial owner owning at least 10% of voting shares may be taxed at 5%; other portfolio dividends at 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding rate is 25% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty relief can reduce interest to 0% or 15% and royalties to 0% for copyright/computer software royalties and 10% for industrial royalties under the Canada-U.S. treaty; rates under other Canadian tax treaties may vary. Arm's-length interest may also qualify for the domestic exemption in subsection 212(3).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory dollar threshold triggers preparation of a mandatory Local File or Master File under Canadian legislation; CRA requires reasonable contemporaneous documentation for all controlled cross-border transactions. Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory for multinational enterprise groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000. Form T106 reporting is required for reportable non-arm's-length transactions once the prescribed CRA reporting thresholds are exceeded, commonly CAD 2,000,000 in aggregate for transactions or loans/advances, and substantial intercompany transactions involving Steam platform royalties or publishing rights should be documented regardless of amount.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Alberta and Canada do not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations. Canada relies on the statutory general anti-avoidance rule (section 245 of the Income Tax Act), the transfer-pricing recharacterization rule (subsection 247(2)), and the OECD Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test to deny treaty or domestic benefits where an entity lacks real commercial substance. A Steam-publishing shell with no Canadian employees, no active decision-making, no IP ownership functions, and no operational risk may be disregarded as a sham, agency, or conduit, and its income may be reallocated or recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Steam/PlayStation payout revenue, creating false expense invoices, falsifying books, signing a knowingly false T2 return, or using undisclosed offshore accounts to hide corporate income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment and recomputation of tax; gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax under subsection 163(2); failure-to-report penalties; daily compounded arrears interest; criminal prosecution under subsection 239(1) with fines from 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 2 years on summary conviction or up to 5 years on indictment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorized false filings may be jointly charged and convicted; the corporate veil may be pierced for fraud; courts may order civil restitution, freeze assets, impose bail conditions including passport surrender and travel bans, and compel restitution of evaded amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length royalties, platform revenue splits, IP licence fees, or cost-sharing amounts with a non-resident parent or associate without contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or using transfer prices inconsistent with functions, assets, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may recharacterize or adjust the transaction under subsection 247(2); transfer pricing penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment where documentation is incomplete, unreliable, or not contemporaneous; reassessment interest and denial of loss/credit offsets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly cause false transfer-pricing records can incur gross-negligence penalties; where the arrangement is a sham, personal liability may attach for conspiracy or fraud; court orders may include restitution, asset freezing, and criminal travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an Alberta corporation with no real economic substance solely to invoice Steam/PlayStation sales, collect treaty-based withholding exemptions, or avoid Canadian tax while all substantive management and control occurs outside Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may disregard the shell under common law sham doctrine, apply section 245 GAAR to deny the tax benefit, reallocate income to the true economic owner, impose gross negligence penalties, reassess Part XIII withholding tax on distributions, and refer the matter for criminal investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the shell is used to perpetrate fraud or evade tax, courts may pierce the corporate veil; directors and shadow directors are exposed to personal civil liability, disqualification orders, travel bans, and penalties for knowing assistance in a criminal tax scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an unregistered money-services business for gaming proceeds, failing to verify beneficial ownership, failing to report a suspicious transaction involving Steam/PlayStation payouts, or structuring transactions to avoid reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for individuals and up to CAD 1,000,000 for entities per violation; criminal liability for laundering the proceeds of crime under the Criminal Code may attract imprisonment and forfeiture of assets; the underlying corporate registration may also be suspended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be held personally liable for civil penalties where they failed to exercise due diligence to prevent the breach; prosecution may lead to individual fines, imprisonment, asset seizure, passport surrender, and travel restrictions while proceedings are pending.
